title: Muse Spark usage
body:
### Provider Name
Muse Spark (Meta)

### Provider Website
https://dev.meta.ai/

### What usage data does this provider expose?
- Local metering, always available: session transcripts with token usage (input/output/cache), prompt and session counts, per-day and per-model breakdowns.
- Subscribed accounts: 5-hour session + 7-day weekly usage percents with reset times, plus tier name, via an authenticated key-endpoint probe. Subscribed without a usage snapshot yet: tier name only.
- Pay-as-you-go: local metering only.


### Will you build the provider?
Yes, I will submit a PR

### Additional Context

Reference implementation: omacom/omarchy#10610.

- Local sources: native `muse` transcripts at `$XDG_DATA_HOME/muse/sessions` (fallback `~/.local/share/muse/sessions`, date-sharded `YYYY/MM/DD/<id>/session.jsonl`, `retained_frame` wrappers with `children[].record_json` payloads, `model_completed` events carry usage) plus opencode rows (`providerID == "meta"`, or `"muse-spark"` in modelID on the `opencode` provider). XDG layout verified on macOS — not `Application Support`.
- Subscription probe: `POST` the Muse key endpoint with the saved OAuth token (`~/.config/muse/auth.json` → `providers.meta.access_token`, Bearer, memory only, never persisted). Read `subs_usage.window` and `subs_usage.weekly` (`used_percent`, `resets_at` epoch) plus `subs_tier_name`.
- States: `is_subs_active=false` with no `subs_usage` = pay-as-you-go, not an error. `401/403` = sign-in expired. Transport failure → retry with backoff. Cache the probe ~60s; don't refetch per UI refresh.

https://commandcode.ai/models/muse-spark-1-2-contributor

## Codex relay-xyz experience — 2026-08-18

I installed `relay-xyz` into the global Codex skills directory as a symlink and ran its required harness locator successfully. The locator found the XYZ Forge harness plus `tick`, Codex, and agy workers.

Commandcode is not yet a first-class relay worker: this checkout ships `codex-turn.sh` and `agy-turn.sh`, but no `commandcode-turn.sh`. I therefore used Commandcode only as a bounded, read-only, plan-mode one-shot reviewer; it could not participate in the serialized `relay-drive.sh` turn protocol.

Results:

- `qwen/qwen3.8-max`: no emitted review after 150 seconds.
- `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`: no emitted review after 120 seconds; interrupted cleanly (exit 130).
- `meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor`: passed a minimal smoke test immediately (`READY`) and completed an inline PR #40 patch review in ~28 seconds. It returned `Changes requested`; two reported blockers were contradicted by live evidence (the ledger has `milestone`, and all eight draft-card title/body updates succeeded). Its remaining comments were useful hardening suggestions: capacity beyond the configured Project list limit, multi-call remote partial-state reporting, and more negative-path coverage.

Recommendation: add a supported `commandcode-turn.sh` adapter before treating Commandcode as a relay participant. Until then, use it for explicitly read-only, bounded patch reviews, ideally with the patch provided inline to avoid tool-orientation stalls.

## Second instance — GH-42 build and third live Muse relay — 2026-08-18

Muse Spark Contributor was asked to build the missing worker using `meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor`. Its first bounded run produced no code; its second, larger run produced the initial Python-authoritative adapter, thin Bash entry point, and mocked test. It reached the turn cap before independently completing the task, so Codex took ownership of the integration and QA.

The third attempt was a real `/relay-xyz` review-only turn in a fresh clone: `RELAY-GH42-MUSE-THIRD`, worktree isolation on, `ALLOW_PATHS` empty, and a 300-second turn timeout. It ran for 3m20s, committed only its permitted relay transcript, and handed the token to the peer. `relay-drive.sh --review-once` returned 5, which means a completed non-approval review (`Changes requested`), not a stalled worker.

Muse's review found two real containment gaps: a failed isolated-worktree setup or off-lane containment path exited before `rtl.enforce`, which could strand an already-claimed token; and Commandcode should always receive the resolved `TICK_REPO_ROOT`. Codex fixed both, gave containment exit 6 priority, switched flags parsing to `shlex.split`, logged otherwise opaque launch exceptions, and added the isolated off-lane handoff regression. One reported token-root concern was broader than the exact isolated path, but the unconditional child-environment fix covers the valid cross-root case.

QA results:

- `test/commandcode-turn.sh`: 20 passed, 0 failed.
- Existing `test/codex-turn.sh`: 43 passed, 0 failed.
- `test/relay-pkg-freshness.sh`: 3 passed, 0 failed.
- Full clean-clone `validate.sh`: 215/216 passed; the only failure was the generated `ROADMAP-DASHBOARD.md` being stale after the new GH-42 working-record pointer. Regenerating that artifact made `test/roadmap-dashboard.sh` pass 9/0. This is documentation-artifact drift, not an adapter failure.

Recommendation: Muse is viable for bounded implementation and useful as a real relay reviewer once wrapped by the supported adapter, but it needs a Codex-owned completion and containment review for safety-critical harness changes. The next PR carries the adapter and the exact QA record above.

— Codex - Terra High

title: [Feature] Muse Spark CLI Support (monthly subscription plan quota via Muse Code)
body:
### Problem / Use Case

OmniRoute currently supports Muse Spark through the Muse Spark API and Muse Spark Web, but there is no way to use the Muse Spark CLI quota included with a Muse Spark subscription.

I'm using a Muse Spark subscription that provides dedicated Muse Code usage/quota. I would like to route requests through OmniRoute using that subscription quota instead of having to use separate API credits or the Web provider.

OmniRoute already supports a similar workflow for subscription-backed coding providers such as Codex and Claude Code. I would like Muse Spark Code to be supported in the same way.

The main use case is:

- Authenticate using the credentials/session supported by the official Muse Spark CLI.
- Use the CLI quota included with the user's Muse Spark subscription.
- Route Muse Spark CLI models through OmniRoute just like other providers.
- Avoid requiring separate Muse Spark API billing when CLI quota is available.

### Proposed Solution

Add a new Muse Spark CLI provider/integration, following the existing Codex and Claude Code integrations in OmniRoute as closely as possible.

Ideally, OmniRoute would:

1. Support authentication using the same account/session mechanism used by the official Muse Spark CLI.
2. Allow Muse Spark CLI to be configured as a provider independently from the existing Muse Spark API and Muse Spark Web providers.
3. Route requests through the Muse Spark CLI/subscription backend so that usage is charged against the subscription's CLI quota rather than API credits.
4. Expose the models available through Muse Spark CLI through the normal OmniRoute model/provider interface.
5. Handle authentication expiration and provider errors consistently with the Codex and Claude Code implementations.
6. Allow Muse Spark CLI to participate in normal OmniRoute routing/fallback configurations.

Where possible, the implementation should reuse the abstractions already created for subscription-backed CLI providers rather than introducing a separate architecture specifically for Muse Spark.

### Alternatives Considered

The current alternatives are:

- Use the Muse Spark API provider and pay for API usage separately.
- Use the existing Muse Spark Web integration.
- Run the official Muse Spark CLI separately from OmniRoute.

These approaches work for some use cases, but they do not allow OmniRoute to make use of the CLI quota already included with a Muse Spark subscription.

Using the CLI separately also means losing OmniRoute features such as centralized routing, provider fallback, model selection, and a unified interface.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Muse Spark CLI is available as a separate provider from Muse Spark API and Muse Spark Web.
- A user with a valid Muse Spark subscription can authenticate/configure the CLI provider.
- Requests sent through the provider use the Muse Spark CLI/subscription quota rather than Muse Spark API credits.
- Models available through Muse Spark CLI can be selected through OmniRoute.
- Standard chat/completion requests work through the provider.
- Authentication/session expiration is detected and produces a useful error or re-authentication flow.
- Muse Spark CLI can be used in normal OmniRoute routing and fallback configurations.
- Existing Muse Spark API and Muse Spark Web integrations continue to work unchanged.
- Existing Codex and Claude Code integrations are not regressed.
- Automated tests cover the new provider's configuration, authentication handling, request routing, and error handling.

### Area

CLI Tools Integration

### Related Provider(s)

Muse Spark

### Additional Context

This is intended to be analogous to OmniRoute's existing Codex and Claude Code support.

The important distinction is that this should not simply be another way of calling the Muse Spark API. The goal is specifically to make use of the CLI usage/quota included with a Muse Spark subscription.

Muse Spark already has an official CLI, so ideally OmniRoute could reuse or integrate with the authentication/session mechanism used by that CLI rather than requiring users to provide separate API credentials.

Keeping Muse Spark API, Muse Spark Web, and Muse Spark CLI as separate provider options would also make it clear which quota/billing mechanism is being used.

### Expected Test Plan

- Add unit tests for Muse Spark CLI provider registration and configuration.
- Add tests for loading and validating Muse Spark CLI authentication/session information.
- Add tests for successful request translation and response handling.
- Add tests for expired/invalid authentication.
- Add tests for provider/network/rate-limit errors.
- Add tests confirming Muse Spark CLI can participate in routing and fallback chains.
- Add regression tests ensuring Muse Spark API and Muse Spark Web behavior is unchanged.
- Keep existing Codex and Claude Code provider tests green.
- Perform an integration/smoke test with a real Muse Spark subscription to confirm requests are successfully served through the CLI subscription path and do not require Muse Spark API credits.

title: Add Meta Muse Spark via Muse Code subscription (bring-your-own-subscription, no Pro required)
body:
## Summary
Add a "Muse Code subscription" entry to the model picker, next to the Claude Code and ChatGPT subscription entries. Users sign in with their Meta account through a device-code flow; usage is billed to their own Muse Code subscription, with no Dyad Pro involvement.

## Motivation
Muse Code subscribers currently have no way to use their subscription inside Dyad. They must either pay per-token via another provider or enable Dyad Pro, even though Meta exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for subscribers.

## Proposal
- Model picker entry "Muse Code subscription" with Meta brand icon and Experimental badge.
- Sign-in via Meta device-code flow (RFC 8628) executed in the main process; minted key stored encrypted in `muse-code-subscription.enc` (same pattern as `codex-subscription.enc`).
- `muse-code` cloud provider (`muse-spark-1.3`) over an OpenAI-compatible client pointed at the Meta API; explicit settings key still takes precedence (manual BYOK keeps working).
- Picker unlock bypass when the subscription is connected, mirroring the Claude Code / ChatGPT bypasses.
- No changes to Pro routing: with Pro credits enabled the standard engine path applies.

Tests included (service, hook, menu, picker, client). No dependency, schema, or migration changes.

## Open questions for maintainers
1. Is an unofficial Meta auth flow acceptable, given it can break without notice?
2. With Pro credits enabled, requests would take the standard engine path with the `muse-code/` prefix. How should that case behave — is gateway support conceivable, or do you prefer an explicit "not supported via Pro" message?
3. Is a separate `.enc` credential file the preferred storage, or should the minted key live in `providerSettings`?

Happy to reshape the implementation based on your feedback before opening a PR.

title: Let the agent find configured models and pick the sub-agent model on request
body:
## Problem
In Agent mode, the sub-agent model is a fixed setting chosen by the user. If I ask the agent to run a sub-agent on a particular model, it can't look up which models I have set up across my providers. It has to guess the exact model ID, and a wrong guess fails with "Model not found".

Example: I asked for a sub-agent on Muse Spark. The agent tried `Muse Spark`, `muse-spark`, `meta/muse-spark` and `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, and every one failed. It had no way to see what the correct ID was.

## Request
1. Give the agent a tool that lists the models configured across all enabled providers, with each model's exact ID and provider.
2. When I name a model in plain words ("use Muse Spark"), the agent looks it up in that list, picks the closest match, and uses that ID for the sub-agent.
3. If there's no clear match, the agent shows the closest options instead of guessing.
4. Keep the Settings default for when I don't name a model, but don't require it to be the only option.

## Use case
Different sub-tasks suit different models: a cheap, fast one for research and a stronger one for harder work. I should be able to say which model to use in the chat and have the agent sort out the exact ID, instead of changing a fixed setting each time.

With no `--model`, `muse exec` runs Muse's catalog default, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, whose catalog entry says content may be used for product improvement. The catalog list labels Muse's own default "(Muse default)".

title: fix: offer catalog models that carry a named profile
body:
## Problem

On Muse 1.3.0 (1.3.0-R3401.1) the model menu shows only the current model, and no catalog model can be selected. Live `model/list` for a Meta account returns:

```
source: providerCatalog
{"modelId":"muse-spark-1.3","providerId":"meta","profileId":"tbh","isDefault":false}
{"modelId":"muse-spark-1.3-contributor","providerId":"meta","profileId":"tbh","isDefault":true}
{"modelId":"muse-spark-1.2","providerId":"meta","profileId":"tbh","isDefault":false}
{"modelId":"muse-spark-1.2-contributor","providerId":"meta","profileId":"tbh","isDefault":false}
```

Every row carries the catalog's profile; the SDK types `ModelListResult.profileId` as "the catalog's profile". `buildConfigOptions` dropped every row with a `profileId`, and `selectModel` and the SDK host refused one, so the menu fell back to the synthetic current-model entry. That entry is the built-in `muse-spark-1.2` unless Muse settings name a model.

This is the "rerun with a real public profile catalog before enabling" step recorded in `docs/capability-audit.md`.

## Changes

1. **Offer catalog models that carry a named profile.** Profiled rows are advertised and selectable. The profile already travels with the selection through `session/setModel` (`muse-sdk-host.ts`), which is then confirmed with `session/read`. `session/read` does not report a profile, so there is no extra profile check.
2. **Default to `muse-spark-1.3`** when neither the session nor Muse settings name a model. This is a separate commit. It deliberately keeps an explicit non-contributor default instead of following the catalog default, which is `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`: that model's catalog description says content "may be used for product improvement", which a user should opt into, not inherit silently.

## Verification

Live, macOS arm64, Muse 1.3.0-R3401.1, branch build (`node dist/index.js`), with no `settings.json` model:

- `session/new`: the model is `muse-spark-1.3`.
- After `/models`, the menu lists `muse-spark-1.3, muse-spark-1.3-contributor, muse-spark-1.2, muse-spark-1.2-contributor`.
- `session/set_config_option` to the profiled `muse-spark-1.2` choice returned OK, and the following turn ended `end_turn`. Muse's session log for that session references only `muse-spark-1.2`, so the profiled selection routed to exactly the chosen model.

Unit tests (`npm run test:unit`), run in a Linux `node:24` container to match CI: this branch and `main` fail the identical 9 tests (`modes`, `mode-config`, `muse-sdk`, `permissions`: bypass-approval and spawn-flag cases, which appear to be environment-related) and pass the rest. The updated `model-identity` and `config-options` tests pass. `npm run check` is clean.

title: feat(zen): route muse-spark models through opencode Responses protocol
body:
## Summary

opencode zen now serves the muse-spark family only through the OpenAI **Responses** protocol: `POST /chat/completions` returns `400 ModelProtocolUnsupported: "Model does not support this protocol."` (verified 2026-09-29 with a valid key; paid `muse-spark-1.3` passes auth and reaches billing, confirming it is protocol-level). This PR routes zen muse-spark models to `POST /zen/v1/responses` and converts both directions back to the chat protocol inside `callZenAPI`, so every downstream entry point (chat, /v1/responses, anthropic) works unchanged.

Protocol mapping follows the official zen endpoint table (GPT/Grok/Muse Spark → Responses, Claude/Qwen → Anthropic, rest → Chat Completions); only muse-spark-* is needed today, `gpt-*`/`grok-*` prefixes are reserved in the table.

## Changes

- **Protocol routing** in `callZenAPI`: `zenUpstreamNeedsResponses` (prefix `muse-spark-*`) selects the `/responses` endpoint; the response is converted back to chat before returning, so callers are unaffected.
- **`buildZenResponsesBody`**: chat → Responses request mapping — system → `instructions`, assistant tool calls → `function_call` items, tool results → `function_call_output`, nested tools → flat format, `max_tokens` → `max_output_tokens` (values 1–15 floored to 128000, same convention as `buildUpstreamBody`, since the Meta backend requires >= 16 and reasoning models burn small budgets on reasoning).
- **Upstream always streams**: `streamZenResponsesAsChat` translates Responses SSE events into `chat.completion.chunk` lines live (reasoning_content, tool_call start/argument deltas, finish_reason, usage, [DONE]); `collapseZenResponsesStream` folds the same event stream into a single chat.completion JSON for non-streaming clients. Watchdog ctx, semaphore, proxy pool, retries and failover accounting are reused as-is.
- **Free-tier agent-shape fix**: with a real key, zen free-tier requests missing *any* of the 5 core tools (`bash/edit/glob/grep/read`) or sent non-streaming get `403 FreeTierError` (verified by matrix test). Core tools are now topped up for **all** zen free requests instead of only anonymous (public key) ones.
- **Tests** (`zen_responses_test.go`): protocol routing, request mapping (incl. clamped/passthrough max tokens, nested tool arguments, anonymous tool top-up), SSE → chat chunk translation (event order, tool args dedup, finish/usage frames) and collapse into chat.completion JSON.

## Testing

- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] Full `go test` suite passes
- [x] Live end-to-end against opencode.ai: `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` returns streamed content ("你好") with role/usage/[DONE] chunks, and collapsed JSON ("再见") via the non-streaming path, through a real key + proxy
- [x] Matrix-tested upstream validation rules (tools count/names, stream requirement) to pin down the 403 FreeTierError semantics

Note: `muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free` is marked deprecated on models.dev; `1.3` remains active. If 1.2 disappears from the upstream list, the periodic zen model sync will drop it automatically.

### Provider claims

- Meta release, published 2026-09-02: https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-spark-1-3
- Meta evaluation methodology, published 2026-09-02: https://research.meta.ai/static/muse-spark-1-3-multimodal-evaluation-methodology

The contributor route materially improves Geist's inexpensive agentic option because it exposes the newer 1.3 behavior at the same $0.10/$0.20 price as the cataloged 1.2 contributor route and requires no new dependency or architecture. It lives here because this was the repository attached to the session. Keeping it on this branch, or moving it to its own repository, avoids mixing it into `main`.

## What changes for the user
- The menu shows **AI: Add to Calendar, AI: Improve, AI: Reply, AI: Reply to Selection, AI: Resume** instead of "Claude: …".
- Each entry asks, in order:

| Situation | Answered by |
|---|---|
| Online | Claude: Claude Code on the subscription, then an Anthropic API key if stored |

What the provider does * **Local spend, no API:** `internal/providers/muse_code/muse_code.go:224` `populateSnapshot` scans `/muse/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD//session.jsonl` (`~/.local/share/muse/sessions` or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/muse/sessions` via `paths.go:resolveSessionsDirs` / `detect/muse_code.go:defaultMuseSessionsDir`) for `model_completed` run events (same `recorded_at` micros, `usage:{input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_tokens/cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, reasoning_tokens}`, `model`; reasoning folds into output). Dedup by canonical path, skip `subagent/` transcripts (`isSubagentTranscript`), price via `pricing.Estimate` (`pricing_supplement.json` `muse-spark-1.3` `$1.25/M in, $4.25/M out` and `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` `$0.10/$0.20`). Sets `total_*`, `muse.session`/ `muse.weekly` quota meters, `ModelUsage` (`AppendModelUsage`), `DailySeries` (`tokens`/`cost`/`sessions`), `total_sessions`/`sessions_today`/`sessions_7d`. `HasCredential` checks `META_API_KEY` env or `auth.json` (`MUSE_CONFIG_DIR`/ `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`~/.config/muse/auth.json` or `MUSE_AUTH_PATH`). `HasChanged` always polls when credentialed (`muse_code.go:95` — quota drifts without local writes, same rationale as `codex`), otherwise scans `*.jsonl` mtimes recursively. * **Live quota (best-effort, never fails Fetch):** `internal/providers/muse_code/quota.go:154` primary `POST https://api.meta.ai/v1/responses` `{model:"muse-spark-1.3-contributor", store:false, stream:true, input:"hi"}` `Authorization: Bearer `, `Accept: text/event-stream`, parses first `event: response.subscription_usage` (`subscription:{tier, weekly:{used_percent,resets_at}, window:{used_percent,resets_at, window_duration_mins}}`) → `applySubscriptionUsage:272` (`muse.session`/`muse.weekly` `Used/Limit` 100, `Resets`, `plan_name` via `quotaPlanName`). Fallback `POST https://dev.meta.ai/api/graphql/` `LLMDCUsageQuery` (`quota.go:466` `postQuotaForm`) with `llm_sess`/`ecto_1_sess` browser cookie (passive `shared.LoadOrRefreshBrowserSession`, `quotaCookieDomain=dev.meta.ai`), `team_id` + volatile `fb_dtsg`/`lsd`/`doc_id` from `quota_tokens_file` JSON (see `docs/MUSE_CODE_GRAPHQL_QUOTA_RESEARCH.md`). Any auth-shaped failure records a `muse_quota_auth` diagnostic (`visit dev.meta.ai in Chrome`) and leaves local spend intact. ## 2. Prior behavior (committed `ab6f48a`/`425943a`) * `muse_code.go` was logs-only: `Fetch` scanned sessions, `buildStatusMessage`, no `enrichQuota`. `widgets.go:8` used `providerbase.CodingToolDashboard` with `GaugePriority` `muse.session/muse.weekly` + `total_*`, `CompactRows` Sessions/Tokens/Cost, but `StandardSectionOrder = CodingToolSectionOrder()` (`Header, TopUsageProgress, ModelBurn, ClientBurn, ToolUsage, MCPUsage, LanguageBurn, CodeStats, OtherData`) and `ShowClientComposition`/`ShowLanguageComposition`/ `ShowCodeStatsComposition`/`ShowActualToolUsage`/`ShowMCPUsage = true` — all empty for `muse_code` (it never sets `client_*`/`project_*`/`tool_*`/`mcp_*`/ `lang_*`/`code_stats`), so `tui/tiles.go:538` `emptyTileSectionContent` rendered `No X data for this time range` for each. `quota.go` not yet present; `muse_code` had no quota. ## 3. What changed (uncommitted in this handoff) * `quota.go` (new, `internal/providers/muse_code/quota.go:1-606`): `responsesBaseURL`, `responsesProbeModel`, `museAPIKeyCache` (`sync.Mutex` `key/ok/set`), `loadMuseAPIKey` (now checks `META_API_KEY` → `~/.config/openusage/muse.json` file → memo → keychain, and best-effort `saveMuseAPIKeyToFile`), `readMuseAPIKeyFromKeychain` (`security find-generic-password -a meta -s ai.meta.dev.credentials -w` `20s` timeout), `postSubscriptionUsage` (SSE, 64K trunc, `parseQuotaExhausted` for `429`), `trySubscriptionUsage`, `enrichQuota`, `quotaForm`/`postQuotaForm`, `applyQuotaMeters`, `quotaSummary`. Added `path/filepath` import. * `muse_code.go:60` `HasChanged` now always polls when credentialed and scans `*.jsonl` mtimes; `Fetch:153` now calls `enrichQuota` + `applyPlanNameOverride`. * `widgets.go:8` `dashboardWidget` now overrides `StandardSectionOrder` to `Header, TopUsageProgress, OtherData` only, and sets `ShowClientComposition=false`, `ShowLanguageComposition=false`, `ShowCodeStatsComposition=false`, `ShowActualToolUsage=false`, `ShowMCPUsage=false` (ModelBurn/DailyUsage hidden — they expect `model_*` metrics while `muse_code` only populates `ModelUsage`/ `DailySeries`). `detailWidget` changed from `CodingToolDetailWidget(false)` to minimal `DetailWidget{Usage, Models, Spending, Trends, Tokens, Activity}` (clients/projects/tools/MCP/language/codeStats hidden). Header tag now correctly shows `Usage` (⚡) when `muse.session` present; previously `total_cost_usd` alone fell through to `Credits` (💰) (`tui/model_display_info.go:396` `hasUsage`). * `tui/provider_widget.go` / `settings_modal_preferences.go` / `quota_test.go` / `has_changed_test.go` / `plan_name_test.go` / `local_auth_hint_test.go` deltas. * `docs/MUSE_CODE_GRAPHQL_QUOTA_RESEARCH.md` updated with implemented client sketch. ## 4. The single password prompt — what the maintainer should know * `~/.config/muse/auth.json` is `{"providers":{"meta":{"storage":"keychain"}}}`, the secret is the keychain blob `{"api_key":"LLM|…","access_token":"dca:…"}`. `loadMuseAPIKey` (`quota.go:117`) is now: ```go META_API_KEY env → ~/.config/openusage/muse.json file (apiKey/api_key/key or plain text) → museAPIKeyCache (sync.Mutex, in-process, one entry) → security find-generic-password ``` The `security` exec prompts for password/Touch ID when the login keychain is locked. The cache makes it at most one prompt per daemon lifetime (the Go `provider.HasChanged` always returns true when credentialed, so every poll would otherwise re-prompt). On first successful keychain read it best-effort persists to `~/.config/openusage/muse.json` (`0o600` via `os.WriteFile` + `os.Rename`, `saveMuseAPIKeyToFile:173`, don't overwrite existing file). Next launch (or the Swift app) hits the file before the keychain, so zero prompts. The file is the same one Swift's `UserAPIKeyStore` (`~/.config/openusage/muse.json`) reads, so the two apps share the cached key. `META_API_KEY` env still wins. First failure (locked/denied) is cached as `("",false)` and never re-prompts until the daemon restarts (same as `museAPIKeyCache` before). ## 5. Quota edge case — exhausted subscription When `Everyday Usage` is exhausted the Responses probe returns ``` HTTP 429 {"error":{"code":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"Subscription quota exhausted. Your usage window resets at 2026-09-14T00:00:00Z.","resets_at":1789344000}} ``` instead of `200` SSE. Previously `postSubscriptionUsage:196` did `return nil,429,fmt.Errorf("HTTP 429…")` → `trySubscriptionUsage:308` set `muse_quota_error` and returned empty, so `muse.session`/`muse.weekly` were missing and `computeDisplayInfo` fell through to `total_cost_usd` → `Credits`. Now `postSubscriptionUsage:196` checks `429` + `parseQuotaExhausted:166` (`code==rate_limit_exceeded` && `message` contains `quota` case-insensitive && `resets_at>0`) and returns `subscriptionUsage{Weekly:100, Window:100, Resets:resets_at, WindowDurationMins:300}`. `applySubscriptionUsage` then emits `muse.session`/ `muse.weekly` `Used:100 Limit:100 Resets:2026-09-14T00:00:00Z`, `quotaSummary` appends `quota session 100% / quota weekly 100%` to `Message`, and the TUI header becomes `Usage` with Session/Weekly 100% gauges and countdowns. Generic `429` without `quota` still returns `requestFailed(429)` and degrades to local spend. ## 6. Branch / PR status Branch `feat/muse-code-provider` on fork `tomck/openusage-go` is at `425943a` (`fork/feat/muse-code-provider` up-to-date). The quota client + file cache + 429 handling + widget slimming are local unstaged/untracked changes (`quota.go`, `quota_test.go`, `has_changed_test.go`, `plan_name_test.go`, `muse_code.go`, `widgets.go`, `provider_widget.go`, `settings_modal_preferences.go`, `local_auth_hint_test.go`, `SPARKTHINKING.md`). No PR has been opened by an agent yet. To open a PR: ```bash git -C openusage-go add internal/providers/muse_code/quota.go internal/providers/muse_code/quota_test.go \ internal/providers/muse_code/has_changed_test.go internal/providers/muse_code/plan_name_test.go \ internal/providers/muse_code/muse_code.go internal/providers/muse_code/widgets.go \ internal/tui/provider_widget.go internal/tui/settings_modal_preferences.go \ internal/tui/local_auth_hint_test.go docs/MUSE_CODE_GRAPHQL_QUOTA_RESEARCH.md git commit -m "Add Muse Code live quota (Responses SSE) with single-prompt file cache and exhausted-quota handling" git push fork feat/muse-code-provider gh pr create --repo janekbaraniewski/openusage --base main --head tomck:feat/muse-code-provider ``` Update `docs/MUSE_CODE_GRAPHQL_QUOTA_RESEARCH.md` and `README` provider table before opening. The daemon must be restarted after `make build` (`pkill -f "openusage telemetry daemon"` + `launchctl kickstart -k` or `install`) — a stale daemon shows `export --source auto` 4h old while `export --source direct` is fresh.

title: feat(ai): add the Muse Code subscription provider via the official muse CLI
body:
## Summary

Adds the `muse-code-subscription` provider: Muse Spark 1.2 and 1.3, plus the contributor variants of both. Each turn runs through the official `muse exec --json` CLI instead of Meta's API.

**Why a CLI sidecar:** Meta's [Model API Terms §3.2](https://dev.meta.ai/legal/terms-of-service) limit a Coding Harness Subscription credential to the coding harness. The [Muse Code subscription docs](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions) say flat-rate use works only through the Muse Code CLI. The earlier revision of this PR minted a key and called `api.meta.ai` directly, and that code is removed. Senpi now never reads, mints, or sends a Meta credential; `muse` owns sign-in (`muse login`), requests, and its own agent tools.

- `api/muse-code-cli.ts` (Node-only, loaded through `api/muse-code-cli.lazy.ts`; `muse-code-cli-provider.ts` provides the static module for Bun binaries):
  - writes the conversation to a mode-0600 temporary prompt file;
  - streams `run_output_delta` events;
  - treats `run_terminal` as completion, because Muse descendants can keep stdout open after the turn ends;
  - then kills the detached process group, and does the same on cancellation.
- The OmO no-tools setting maps to `--disable-shell --disable-write`.
- An api-key resolver marks the provider available without holding any secret.

## Verification

- `bun run check`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-pr-changelog.mjs`: PASS.
- `packages/ai`: `muse-code-cli.test.ts` covers the held-stdout regression, a failed CLI, and a pre-cancelled turn. With the catalog, fork-owned catalog, and model-shard tests, 19/19 pass.
- `packages/coding-agent`: `test/bun/runtime-modules.test.ts` passes 2/2.
- Live QA with a clean agent dir and real `muse` 1.3.0: `senpi --model muse-code-subscription/muse-spark-1.2 --print "Use your own file-read tool to read …/package.json …"` returned the package name and exited 0.

title: feat(harness): add the Muse provider
body:
## What changed

Muse Code is a live harness now, in the same shape as the other CLI providers. A turn is one `muse exec --json` child. Resume uses the session id Muse already minted, and the next send waits until that process has actually exited, because the CLI keeps the session lock until then. The picker reads `model/list` from a short `muse serve` probe and falls back to the built-in Spark list when the CLI isn't there. Sign-in is `muse login`. The icon is the Meta mark.

The turn trusts the workspace so project skills and rules load, and it does not pass `--yolo` or `--disable-sandbox`. Full access stops approval prompts and leaves the OS sandbox on. The other access modes fail closed: `muse exec` has no way to answer a prompt mid-run, and leaving the default approval mode on will sit there forever. `none` and `ultra` are never sent. `max` goes out only for standard `muse-spark-1.3`.

User skills are picked up from `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/muse/skills`, or `~/.config/muse/skills` when that isn't set. They do not override `.agents/skills`.

Two small fixes came with it so `npm run check` stays quiet on this machine: a test setup that installs web storage without touching Node's warning getter, and a clippy rewrite of the control-grant check.

## Why

I wanted Muse in the picker without inventing a protocol the headless CLI doesn't have. Project skills stay unloaded until the workspace is trusted, `max` is a 400 on Spark 1.2 and on the contributor ids, and a dangerous shell under `on-request` blocks with nothing on stdout to reply to. The adapter follows those limits.

## UI

Muse shows up in the harness list with the Meta mark. No other chrome moved.

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `npm run check` (3236 web tests and `tsc` clean; `cargo fmt`, clippy `-D warnings`, and 393 Rust tests clean)
- [x] This PR is small and focused
- [x] I did not mix unrelated changes

title: [Provider API] Region-restricted models return 403 "Authentication failed" while the same API correctly returns MODEL_NOT_IN_PLAN for plan gates
body:
### Summary

The Provider API does not map regional restrictions to a useful error. For region-blocked models it
returns a credential-shaped error, while the CLI reports the real cause for the same account, and
while the API itself handles a plan gate correctly.

Same account, same endpoint, same key, only `model` differs:

- `meta/muse-spark-1.2` -> 403 {"error":{"message":"Authentication failed. Please check your credentials.","type":"permission_error"}}
- `meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` -> same auth-shaped 403
- `meta/muse-spark-1.1` -> 403 {"error":{"message":"MODEL_NOT_IN_PLAN: Muse Spark 1.1 available in Pro and above plans or extra on demand usage","type":"permission_error","code":"FORBIDDEN"}}
- `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` -> 200 OK

CLI 1.65.2, same account:
  cmd -p "hi" -m meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor
  -> Error: 403 meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor is not available in your region per Meta's Geographic
     Use Policy. https://ai.developer.meta.com/legal/geographic-use-policy  (exit code 4)

So the region reason is known internally, the plan gate is already reported correctly, but the API
collapses the regional case into "Authentication failed". Clients that only use the Provider API
cannot distinguish a region block from bad credentials, which cost significant debugging time.

### Expected Behavior

Region-blocked models should return a distinct, actionable 403, consistent with the CLI, e.g.:

403 {"error":{
  "message":"meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor is not available in your region per Meta's Geographic Use Policy.",
  "type":"permission_error",
  "code":"MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_REGION"}}

Plan gates must keep returning MODEL_NOT_IN_PLAN (already correct for muse-spark-1.1), and
401 authentication_error "Invalid 'Authorization' header or token." stays reserved for missing or
invalid credentials.

### Actual Behavior

Provider API, region-blocked model:
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":{"message":"Authentication failed. Please check your credentials.","type":"permission_error"}}
x-trace-id: fac34145854a6ab16cd08ad2c905a1fc

Provider API, plan gate (same key — proof the mapping can be correct):
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":{"message":"MODEL_NOT_IN_PLAN: Muse Spark 1.1 available in Pro and above plans or extra on demand usage","type":"permission_error","code":"FORBIDDEN"}}

CLI 1.65.2, region-blocked model (the correct reason the API is missing):
Error: 403 meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor is not available in your region per Meta's Geographic Use
Policy. Read more at https://ai.developer.meta.com/legal/geographic-use-policy. Please try a different model.
exit code: 4

Control:
curl  ... model=deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash -> 200 OK   (x-trace-id: b204db5162a803c8ccb910c9e432aa8e)
cmd -p "reply with exactly: OK" -m deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash -> "OK", exit 0

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. cmd -p "hi" -m meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor        -> region error, exit 4  (correct)
2. curl ... -d '{"model":"meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor", ...}' -> 403 "Authentication failed" (wrong)
3. curl ... -d '{"model":"meta/muse-spark-1.1", ...}'     -> 403 MODEL_NOT_IN_PLAN (correct)
4. curl ... -d '{"model":"deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash", ...}' -> 200 OK

### Command Code Version

1.65.2

### Operating System

Windows

### Terminal/IDE

VS Code + curl 8.21.0 (Windows, Schannel)

### Shell

PowerShell 5.1

### Session file (optional)

N/A — reproduced headlessly (cmd -p), exit codes 4 and 0

### Fix prompt (optional)

The Provider API collapses regional model restrictions into an authentication error, while the
same API reports plan gates correctly and the CLI knows the real reason.

Reproduce

1) CLI 1.65.2:
   cmd -p "hi" -m meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor
   -> exit 4
      Error: 403 meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor is not available in your region per Meta's
      Geographic Use Policy. Read more at https://ai.developer.meta.com/legal/geographic-use-policy.
      Please try a different model.

2) Provider API, same model, same account:
   POST /provider/v1/chat/completions
   -> 403 {"error":{"message":"Authentication failed. Please check your credentials.","type":"permission_error"}}

3) Provider API, plan gate (same key) — already correct, must not regress:
   meta/muse-spark-1.1
   -> 403 {"error":{"message":"MODEL_NOT_IN_PLAN: Muse Spark 1.1 available in Pro and above plans
      or extra on demand usage","type":"permission_error","code":"FORBIDDEN"}}

Where it lives

- The Provider API error-mapping layer that turns gate/upstream failures into the OpenAI error
  envelope for /provider/v1/chat/completions and /provider/v1/responses.
- The regional check already produces a user-facing message for the CLI — reuse that same source of
  truth as the mapped API message instead of a generic auth fallback.

Required behaviour

1. Region restriction -> HTTP 403 with a distinct code and the policy message, e.g.
   {"error":{"message":"<model> is not available in your region per Meta's Geographic Use Policy.
   <docs url>","type":"permission_error","code":"MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_REGION"}}
2. Keep existing plan gates as-is (403 MODEL_NOT_IN_PLAN) — do not change muse-spark-1.1 behaviour.
3. Reserve 401 authentication_error "Invalid 'Authorization' header or token." strictly for missing
   or invalid credentials; never use an auth message for an entitlement/region decision.
4. Keep the mapping provider-agnostic: the same rule should apply to any future region-restricted
   model, not just Meta's.

Tests to add

- valid key + meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor -> 403 with code MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_REGION
  (must NOT contain "Authentication failed")
- valid key + meta/muse-spark-1.1 -> 403 MODEL_NOT_IN_PLAN (unchanged)
- valid key + deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash -> 200
- missing/invalid key -> 401 authentication_error
- regression test asserting the Provider API reason matches the CLI reason for the same
  model/region, so the two surfaces cannot diverge again
- docs update: add the region-restricted models to the "Geo model limits" list and document the
  new error code on the Provider API errors table

Manual verification

- curl valid key + meta/muse-spark-1.2 -> region code/message
- cmd -p "hi" -m meta/muse-spark-1.2 -> same reason, exit 4
- curl valid key + deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash -> 200

### Additional context

Environment

- Provider API: https://api.commandcode.ai/provider/v1
- Command Code CLI: 1.65.2 (Windows), headless via `cmd -p`
- curl 8.21.0 (Windows, Schannel); Windows 11 (build 26200)
- Client region: Indonesia; requests egress via Cloudflare HKG edge
  (CF-RAY a4087d2c7de25df6-HKG / a4088b202c4f2119-HKG)
- Account: putrakoe — plan GOAT (inferred: google/gemini-3.8-flash "GOAT and above" -> 200;
  google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite "Pro and above" -> 403 MODEL_NOT_IN_PLAN)
- No proxy, no TLS interception, no x-cmd-zdr
- Keys tested (masked): prefix user_5GUYVTfML… (len 93, API/VS Code) and
  prefix user_4onCMncue… (len 93, CLI credential cli-2026-09-10). Both behave identically.

Full gate matrix (same account, same keys, same endpoint)

| Model | CLI 1.65.2 | Provider API | Reality |
|---|---|---|---|
| meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor | 403 region msg (exit 4) | 403 permission_error "Authentication failed" | region block |
| meta/muse-spark-1.3 | 403 region msg (exit 4) | 403 permission_error "Authentication failed" | region block |
| meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor | 403 region msg (exit 4) | 403 permission_error "Authentication failed" | region block |
| meta/muse-spark-1.2 | 403 region msg (exit 4) | 403 permission_error "Authentication failed" | region block |
| meta/muse-spark-1.1 | 403 MODEL_NOT_IN_PLAN (exit 4) | 403 MODEL_NOT_IN_PLAN (code FORBIDDEN) | plan gate — API correct |
| deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash | OK (exit 0) | 200 OK | works |
| xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash | — | 200 OK | works |
| z-ai/glm-5.3-flash | — | 200 OK | works |
| xai/grok-4.5 | — | 200 OK | works |
| google/gemini-3.8-flash | — | 200 OK | works |

Key observation: the API maps the plan gate correctly (muse-spark-1.1) but maps the region gate to
an authentication error (muse-spark-1.2 / 1.3 / *-contributor). The CLI has the correct reason for
the same requests, so this is a mapping gap, not missing information.

Verbatim evidence

Provider API, region-blocked model:
  HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
  {"error":{"message":"Authentication failed. Please check your credentials.","type":"permission_error"}}
  x-trace-id: fac34145854a6ab16cd08ad2c905a1fc   (2026-09-25T07:59:21Z, CF-RAY a4087d2c7de25df6-HKG)
  x-trace-id: a2477a186eaaa50c6f1d7d2cbcf170f2   (2026-09-25T08:08:52Z, models list call, 200)

CLI, region-blocked model:
  $ cmd -p "hi" -m meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor
  Error: 403 meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor is not available in your region per Meta's Geographic
  Use Policy. Read more at https://ai.developer.meta.com/legal/geographic-use-policy. Please try a
  different model.
  exit code: 4

CLI, control (same account/key):
  $ cmd -p "Reply with exactly: DEEPSEEK OK" -m deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
  DEEPSEEK OK
  exit code: 0
  $ cmd -p "Berapa 17 x 3? Jawab hanya angkanya." -m deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
  51
  exit code: 0

Provider API, control:
  curl ... -d '{"model":"deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash", ...}' -> 200 OK
  x-trace-id: b204db5162a803c8ccb910c9e432aa8e

`cmd --list-models` lists all five meta/muse-spark-* entries with no region annotation, so the
restriction is only discoverable at request time.

Documentation references

- Geo model limits: https://commandcode.ai/docs/resources/pricing-limits#geo-model-limits
  States "Some providers restrict where their models can be used. If a model is blocked in your
  region, it won't be available to you." but lists only GPT-5.6 Luna and Gemini 3.7 Flash
  ("unavailable in China"). The meta/muse-spark-* family is missing, even though the CLI reports a
  regional block for it.
- Provider API errors: https://commandcode.ai/docs/provider#errors
  Maps 403 to upgrade_required and 401 to authentication_error; no code exists for a regional
  restriction, which is likely why the API falls back to an auth-shaped message.
- Meta Geographic Use Policy: https://ai.developer.meta.com/legal/geographic-use-policy
- CLI error codes / headless exit codes: https://commandcode.ai/docs/troubleshooting/errors

Timeline on this account for meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor

- 2026-09-03  streamed successfully
- 2026-09-22  "You have insufficient credits to make this request."
- 2026-09-25  403 — CLI reports the regional restriction; Provider API reports "Authentication failed"

Requests

1. Map regional restrictions to a distinct Provider API error (suggested code
   MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_REGION) with the same message the CLI already shows.
2. Keep MODEL_NOT_IN_PLAN behaviour unchanged (currently correct).
3. Add the region-restricted models to the "Geo model limits" documentation list, with the
   affected regions.
4. Document the region error code on the Provider API errors table so clients can distinguish
   credential, plan, and region failures.

Available on request: full transcripts for every request above, additional trace IDs, and the full
API keys through a private channel for account lookup. Keys are intentionally masked here.

6. **Live-confirm the endpoint, model list, and pricing before advertising.** Upstream is OPEN. Treat its model names, base URL, and rate card as untrusted until verified against a real response. If the live response disagrees, the catalog must be corrected before merge.
7. Do NOT touch `meta-llama.js:2-5` or any `meta`-aliased code path. `meta-llama` is preserved as-is.

title: Console Go (Meta Muse Spark): MCP tool schemas deeper than 10 levels are rejected, no Meta/Muse sanitizer
body:
## Summary

Muse Spark via OpenCode Go fails on the first request when any tool schema nests deeper than 10 levels. The provider rejects the whole request, not just the offending tool.

```
Error from provider (Console Go): Upstream request failed: [invalid_request_error] JSON schema exceeds the maximum nesting depth of 10 levels
```

- Endpoint: `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses`
- Model: `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` (provider `opencode-go`)
- Provider response body: `{"model":"muse-spark-1.3-contributor","error":{"param":"parameters","type":"invalid_request_error","message":"Error from provider (Console Go): Upstream request failed: [invalid_request_error] JSON schema exceeds the maximum nesting depth of 10 levels"}}`
- opencode 1.18.31

Other models on the same provider (for example `deepseek-v4.1-flash`) accept the same tool schemas, so this only breaks on strictly validating upstreams.

## Reproduction

1. Enable an MCP server with deep tool schemas. The public Vercel MCP server (`https://mcp.vercel.com`) is a minimal example. I measured all 212 published `inputSchema`s by counting object/array member recursion (`properties`, `items`, `additionalProperties`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `allOf`, `$defs`). Twelve reach depth 10 or more:

| tool | depth | bytes | deepest path |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `create_flag` | 14 | 10234 | `.requestBody.environments.oneOf[0].additionalProperties.rules.items.conditions.items.rhs.anyOf[0].items.items.anyOf[0].label` |
| `update_flag` | 13 | 10346 | `.requestBody.environments.additionalProperties.rules.items.conditions.items.rhs.anyOf[0].items.items.anyOf[0].label` |
| `update_sandbox` | 12 | 14775 | `.requestBody.networkPolicy.oneOf[1].allow.oneOf[1].additionalProperties.items.match.queryString.items.key.exact` |
| `update_flag_segment` | 12 | 4471 | `.requestBody.data.rules.items.conditions.items.rhs.anyOf[0].items.items.anyOf[0].label` |
| `create_sandboxes_v4` | 12 | 17019 | `.requestBody.networkPolicy.oneOf[1].allow.oneOf[1].additionalProperties.items.match.queryString.items.key.exact` |
| `create_sandboxes_v3` | 12 | 16836 | `.requestBody.networkPolicy.oneOf[1].allow.oneOf[1].additionalProperties.items.match.queryString.items.key.exact` |
| `create_sandboxes_v2` | 12 | 17156 | `.requestBody.networkPolicy.oneOf[1].allow.oneOf[1].additionalProperties.items.match.queryString.items.key.exact` |
| `update_session_network_policy` | 11 | 10708 | `.requestBody.oneOf[1].allow.oneOf[1].additionalProperties.items.match.queryString.items.key.exact` |
| `update_project` | 11 | 24296 | `.requestBody.trustedSources.anyOf[0].projects.additionalProperties.customAllow.items.to.anyOf[0].slugs.items` |
| `put_firewall_config` | 11 | 9543 | `.requestBody.rules.items.action.mitigate.rateLimit.anyOf[0].anyOf[0].action.anyOf[0].anyOf[0]` |
| `update_firewall_config` | 10 | 19348 | `.requestBody.oneOf[0].value.conditionGroup.items.conditions.items.value.anyOf[1].items` |
| `create_connector` | 10 | 53316 | `.requestBody.anyOf[0].data.anyOf[0].serverConfig.jwks.keys.items.key_ops.items` |

2. Config:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "vercel": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.vercel.com", "enabled": true, "oauth": {} }
  }
}
```

3. `opencode run -m opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor "Reply with exactly: ok"` fails with the error above.
4. The same command with `"mcp": {}` returns `ok`.
5. The same command with only the Vercel MCP enabled fails again, so the MCP server is the trigger.

## Cause

`packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts` has per-provider schema sanitizers for OpenAI, Moonshot/Kimi, and Gemini, but nothing Meta/Muse-shaped. MCP tool schemas are forwarded as published, so any MCP server over the limit breaks every Muse Spark session. Meta's Model API rejects both recursive `$ref` (#45800, #48151) and schemas over its nesting limit.

## Ask

Add a Meta/Muse-bound sanitizer that flattens tool schemas under the provider's nesting limit and strips recursive `$ref`, the same way the other providers are handled.

## Workaround

Disable the offending MCP server for Muse Spark. A dedicated agent keeps the server available for other models:

```json
{
  "agent": {
    "muse": {
      "mode": "primary",
      "model": "opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor",
      "permission": { "vercel_*": "deny" }
    }
  }
}
```

## Related

- #45800 Recursive `$ref` in postgres tool schemas breaks Meta Muse Spark
- #48151 Console Go -> Meta: sanitize recursive `$ref` tool schemas
- #25495 Moonshot/Kimi K2.6 rejects tool schemas with nesting depth > 10

## Problem
After #1 proves the spoken conversation loop on Mentra Live with OpenAI realtime voice, Andrew wants to try Meta's Muse models through the same glasses and compare the two. Mentra Live has no display, so this is audio only.

Muse is offered through Meta Model API (https://dev.meta.ai/, docs at https://ai.developer.meta.com/docs/overview; base URL `https://api.meta.ai/v1`, bearer key). Based on those docs, it doesn't appear to offer a single speech-in, speech-out realtime session the way OpenAI does. The listed pieces are Muse Spark (text and agent model, OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses APIs) and Muse Voice Transcribe (speech to text with turn detection). A Muse agent will likely need a chained pipeline: speech to text, then Muse Spark, then text to speech.

## User-visible outcome
In the prototype app, Andrew can pick "OpenAI" or "Muse" as the agent, start a session, and hold a spoken back-and-forth conversation with Muse through the glasses' mic and speaker, just as with OpenAI in #1.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Muse plugs in through the agent seam built in #1, with no changes to the glasses connection or audio routing code beyond what the seam needs.
- [ ] The phone has a simple agent picker (OpenAI or Muse), and switching agents doesn't require rebuilding the app.
- [ ] With Muse selected, Andrew speaks into the glasses, Muse Spark generates the reply, and the reply is spoken through the glasses' speaker.
- [ ] Multi-turn conversation works, and Muse keeps context across turns within a session.
- [ ] The Meta Model API key is never committed. The README explains how to supply it locally, next to the OpenAI key.
- [ ] The README documents the Muse pipeline and roughly how its response delay compares with OpenAI realtime.

## Out of scope
- Muse Code, Muse Image, SAM, and Muse Glimmer (local models).
- Tools or function calling, wake words, and any backend or token server.
- Android, distribution, and CI.
- Any other agents beyond OpenAI and Muse.

- Speech-to-text path for Muse (Muse Voice Transcribe versus another option).
- Text-to-speech path, since Muse doesn't appear to have its own speech output.
- Which Muse Spark model version to default to.

## Assumptions
- "Meta Muse" means Meta's Muse Spark models on Meta Model API, confirmed by Andrew on 2026-09-28.
- Andrew will create his own Meta Model API key.
- This depends on #1 being merged first.

body:
## Description

`openrouter/meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` fails every turn with `400 Provider returned error` when the resolved thinking level is `max`. The omp log only shows the wrapped error; replaying the exact saved request body directly against `POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/responses` (bypassing omp) surfaces the upstream body:

```json
{"error":{"message":"Provider returned error","code":400,"metadata":{"raw":"{\"error\":{\"code\":null,\"message\":\"The request contains invalid parameters. Check the request body for any errors or inconsistencies.\",\"param\":null,\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\"}}","provider_name":"Meta","is_byok":false}}}
```

The same body with only `reasoning.effort` changed from `max` to `xhigh` returns `HTTP 200 completed` with real `encrypted_content`. This is a strong working hypothesis that OpenRouter/Meta currently rejects `effort: "max"` for this model id — not a claim about all Muse variants.

This is distinct from the earlier synthetic-placeholder failure (`Referenced reasoning item 'rs_...' was not found or has expired`, from ID-bearing `reasoning unavailable` items synthesized in assistant tool-call history). The current failing requests contain zero `type: "reasoning"` items and zero `rs_*` ids in `input`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `omp -p --no-session --model "openrouter/meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor" --thinking max "Reply with exactly OK"` — fails with repeated 400s (raw request saved under `~/.omp/logs/http-400-requests/`).
2. Same command with `--thinking xhigh` — `200 OK`, exits 0.
3. Minimal upstream replay of the saved body (single `input` item, `store: false`, `stream: false`, `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, `reasoning: {"effort": "max", "summary": "auto"}`) → HTTP 400 with the Meta `invalid_request_error` above.
4. Identical replay with `reasoning: {"effort": "xhigh", "summary": "auto"}` → HTTP 200 `status: "completed"`.

Saved failing params (example `1789646932181-3957muv565yr5.json`): `input_len: 1`, `reasoning_items: 0`, `rs_ids: []`, `reasoning: {"effort": "max", "summary": "auto"}`, `store: false`, `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, 12 tools.

## Expected Behavior

The resolved effort ladder for `openrouter/meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` should not offer `max`, since the backend rejects it. `xhigh` works and matches the direct `muse-code` catalog entry for `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` (ladder ends at `xhigh`; `max` exists only on the non-contributor `muse-spark-1.3`).

Suggested fix: narrow provider-level selector in `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/providers/openrouter.kdl` — add `models "meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor" { thinking-efforts "minimal" "low" "medium" "high" "xhigh" }`, leaving `meta/muse-spark-1.3` untouched. Note per `resolve.ts` layering ("explicit spec thinking wins"), a reviewed KDL ladder only constrains the resolved ladder when discovery does not supply its own explicit `thinking.efforts` — OpenRouter live discovery (`mapOpenRouterThinking` in `openai-compat.ts`) maps `supported_efforts` from the wire, so if the endpoint advertises `max` the KDL cap may need to apply at the request-mapping layer instead. Regenerate `rules.json` via `bun run gen:compat` and cover with a resolved-ladder + serialized-request regression test.

## Error Output

```
400 Provider returned error
raw-http-request=/home/dev/.omp/logs/http-400-requests/1789646932181-3957muv565yr5.json
```

Upstream (direct replay, omp bypassed):

```
HTTP 400 {"error":{"message":"Provider returned error","code":400,"metadata":{"raw":"{\"error\":{\"code\":null,\"message\":\"The request contains invalid parameters. Check the request body for any errors or inconsistencies.\",\"param\":null,\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\"}}","provider_name":"Meta","is_byok":false}}}
```

## Platform

Linux

## omp version

18.2.4

## Bun version

1.3.14

## Provider

OpenRouter

## Area

Model selection

## Additional context

- `openrouter:pseudo-api` cache advertises `max` for `meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` (`thinking.efforts: [minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max]`), while the direct `muse-code` entry for `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` caps at `xhigh`.
- Classes rule (`classes/meta.kdl`) already keeps contributor revisions on the 5-tier ladder (`muse-spark-1.3` alone gets `max`); the OpenRouter provider path does not inherit that cap because live discovery supplies explicit thinking.
- Local workaround: pin `openrouter/meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor:xhigh` in `modelRoles`/`fallbackChains` (verified `OK`, exit 0).

# Add Meta Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor as m2c's second worker backend

## Target

Add a second real m2c worker:

- provider/backend: Meta Model API
- model: `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`
- preferred execution client: Codex CLI using Meta's OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoint
- reasoning effort: `high` by default for the initial profile
- API credential source: `MODEL_API_KEY`
- base URL: `https://api.meta.ai/v1`

The user already has Meta Model API access and the dashboard exposes Codex configuration for this model.

## Architectural rule

m2c owns jobs. Workers perform jobs.

The controller must remain backend-neutral.

The Meta worker must implement the same normalized worker contract introduced by 0.2. It must not teach GitHub Watch, queueing, delivery verification, receipts, stats, or result classification any Meta-specific logic.

If adding Meta requires controller conditionals such as `if worker == meta` scattered through orchestration code, stop and improve the worker boundary instead.

Prefer Codex CLI as the execution harness for the first Meta backend.

Reason:
- Meta directly supports the OpenAI Responses protocol.
- The user's Meta dashboard explicitly provides Codex configuration.
- m2c should not grow its own agent/tool loop when a proven execution client can own tool dispatch.
- MiMo's textual pseudo-tool problem is provider-specific and must not be generalized to Meta without evidence.

Do not silently fall back from Meta to MiMo or another provider.

## Credential isolation

Never commit, log, echo, or serialize the Meta API key.

Use local m2c-owned credential/config state or environment injection.

Expected variable:

```text
MODEL_API_KEY
```

Doctor/status output may report configured/missing but must never print the key.

Flight recorder must record only backend/model identity and safe operational metadata.

## Backend identity

Use clear vocabulary approximately:

```text
worker: meta
profile: contributor
mode: build
model: muse-spark-1.3-contributor
reasoning_effort: high
```

Exact field names may follow whatever 0.2 actually lands.

Do not overload OpenCode `agent` terminology.

## Initial scope

Implement only one Meta model/profile initially:

`muse-spark-1.3-contributor`

Do not add every Muse model in the first packet.

Make the model catalogue/extensibility obvious enough that standard Muse Spark can be added later without redesign.

## CLI / jobspec behaviour

After integration, a backend-neutral GitHub job should be able to request Meta through the 0.2 jobspec syntax.

Illustrative only, adapt to the exact 0.2 schema that lands:

```yaml
worker: meta
profile: contributor
mode: build
budget_minutes: 45
```

m2c must deterministically map that profile to `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`.

Unknown Meta profiles fail closed.

Unavailable credential/backend fails BLOCKED with a useful reason.

No automatic routing.

## Capability probe

Add a small explicit health/probe path that can verify:

- Meta backend configured
- Codex executable available
- model/provider config can be constructed
- optional live probe only when explicitly requested
- no secrets printed

Do not make ordinary offline tests perform paid API calls.

## Tool-use acceptance test

The important proof is not plain inference.

Use a bounded live smoke test that requires at least one real filesystem/tool action in an isolated temporary repository, then mechanically verify the effect.

For example:

1. create isolated temp repo
2. ask Meta worker to create one small deterministic file
3. verify file content mechanically
4. verify process/tool result is structured and attributable to this run
5. clean up

Do not accept worker prose saying it used tools as proof.

## m2c integration acceptance

The Meta backend must work through the same controller path as MiMo:

- admission
- isolated checkout
- immutable jobspec
- budget
- timeout/closeout
- runner result
- delivery verification
- flight recorder
- compact receipt
- status/stats
- GitHub finalization

No Meta-specific bypass around delivery truth.

## Cross-platform

Default target is Windows + Linux/WSL.

No hard-coded PowerShell.
No drive-letter assumptions.
No Windows-only shell semantics.

Codex/provider setup must be generated in a platform-neutral way where practical.

## Contributor tier guardrail

Treat `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` as a distinct profile, not just an alias for standard Muse Spark.

Document that it is a different service tier and keep the profile visible in receipts/stats so jobs can later be separated by tier.

Do not route confidential/sensitive workloads to Contributor automatically. m2c does no automatic routing in this release.

## Tests

At minimum:

- worker registry discovers Meta adapter
- Meta contributor profile resolves deterministically
- unknown profile fails closed
- missing API key reports unavailable/BLOCKED
- API key never appears in logs, JSONL, receipts, errors, or doctor output
- generated provider config contains correct endpoint/model but not secret
- reasoning effort defaults to high
- controller code does not require Meta-specific branch logic
- offline test suite uses no real API
- bounded live smoke test is explicit
- Windows CI passes
- Ubuntu CI passes
- existing MiMo regressions remain green

## Documentation

Document:

- how to enable the Meta backend
- required `MODEL_API_KEY`
- selected model: `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`
- how to request it in a job
- how to run the explicit live health check
- that it is optional
- that no provider fallback occurs
- that Contributor is surfaced as its own profile

## Versioning

Follow the standing release rule:

When this backend change is merged and becomes the version being used, bump the program version in the same release flow.

Do not leave a materially changed live m2c wearing the prior version number.

## Delivery contract

Before reporting complete:

- full local tests
- existing formatting/static checks
- explicit Meta live tool smoke test if credential is available
- commit
- push
- remote SHA == local HEAD
- clean worktree
- PR opened
- Windows CI green
- Ubuntu CI green
- do not merge
- report exact SHA and test counts

No push = not complete.

## Design test

The successful outcome is not merely “Muse works.”

The successful outcome is:

> Meta Muse Spark can be added without changing what the m2c controller fundamentally is.

That is the first real proof of the 0.2 worker abstraction.

title: Support Muse Spark through Meta Model API and evaluate the announced open-weight path
body:
## Outcome

Run current Muse Spark models in Finch through a supported hosted provider, with deterministic protocol tests and an explicit path for evaluating local inference only after Meta publishes usable open weights.

## Current evidence (2026-09-02)

- Meta ships **Muse Code**, its own terminal coding agent, powered by Muse Spark: https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-code-and-muse-spark-1-2
- Muse Spark 1.3 is available through **Meta Model API** and Muse Code: https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-spark-1-3
- OpenCode supports Muse Spark through **OpenCode Zen** using an OpenAI Responses-compatible endpoint: https://opencode.ai/docs/zen
- Meta says an open-weights release is planned, but weights are not the current supported delivery path. Do not claim ONNX or local support until an artifact and license can be inspected.

## Scope

### Hosted support

- Add a first-class Meta Model API provider/profile for the current Muse Spark model family.
- Determine and document authentication, endpoint, model discovery, reasoning controls, streaming events, tool calls, structured output, cancellation, retries, rate limits, and error mapping.
- Prefer direct Meta Model API access; optionally support OpenCode Zen through Finch generic Responses-provider configuration without coupling Finch to the OpenCode harness.
- Keep provider credentials in Finch-owned storage and fail closed across provider/audience boundaries.

### Future open-weight investigation

When Meta publishes Muse Spark weights:

- Record the authoritative artifact, revision, checksums, license, tokenizer/config, architecture, and hardware requirements.
- Establish whether direct Candle or ONNX Runtime execution is technically and legally supported.
- If ONNX is viable, add a reproducible export/conversion workflow with pinned tool versions, opset, dynamic axes, quantization policy, and output checksums.
- Do not present conversion success as end-to-end Finch conformance; separately verify generation, streaming, tool use, context limits, cancellation, restart behavior, and resource bounds.
- If Muse Spark is not practical locally, document the evidence and keep hosted support independent.

## Acceptance gates

- Production-boundary tests cover request shape, authentication audience, streaming text, tool calls, model identity, cancellation, malformed events, retry/refresh behavior, and actionable diagnostics.
- A live ignored acceptance test documents required credentials and verifies the current Meta model ID without storing secrets.
- Provider docs distinguish direct Meta API, OpenCode Zen, Muse Code, and any future local artifact.
- Dated conformance evidence is recorded before Finch claims Muse Spark support.
- Link results into the multi-provider conformance work in #98.

## Non-goals

- Reimplementing Muse Code.
- Scraping credentials or subscription state from Muse Code or OpenCode.
- Assuming that Muse Spark replaces Llama in Finch local inference.
- Promising ONNX support before open weights and conversion rights exist.

title: Codex Apps generate tool names >64 chars, causing Meta Muse Spark 1.3 Responses requests to fail with HTTP 400

labels.name: exec
labels.description: Issues related to the `codex exec` subcommand

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: custom-model

body:
## Summary

When using `meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` through OpenRouter in Codex, requests fail with HTTP 400 whenever Codex Apps are enabled.

The provider error is:

```text
Provider returned error

{"error":{"message":"Provider returned error","code":400,"metadata":{"raw":"{\"error\":{\"code\":null,\"message\":\"\`name\` must be at most 64 characters, got 66\",\"param\":\"name\",\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\"}}","provider_name":"Meta","is_byok":false}}}
```

Disabling Codex Apps with:

```text
-c 'features.apps=false'
```

makes the exact same request succeed.

This appears to be caused by Codex Apps exposing namespaced tools whose flattened function names exceed Meta's 64-character tool/function name limit.

## Environment

```text
Codex: OpenAI Codex v0.155.0-alpha.2.6
OS: macOS
Provider: OpenRouter
Model: meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor
API: Responses API
```

Provider configuration:

```toml
model_provider = "openrouter"
model = "meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor"

[model_providers.openrouter]
name = "OpenRouter"
base_url = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"
wire_api = "responses"

[model_providers.openrouter.auth]
command = "/usr/bin/security"
args = ["find-generic-password", "-s", "codex-openrouter", "-w"]
```

## Reproduction

### 1. Normal Codex execution

```bash
codex exec \
  -m meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor \
  --skip-git-repo-check \
  "Reply with exactly: hello"
```

Result:

```text
OpenAI Codex v0.155.0-alpha.2.6
--------
model: meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor
provider: openrouter
--------

ERROR: {"error":{"message":"Provider returned error","code":400,"metadata":{"raw":"{\"error\":{\"code\":null,\"message\":\"\`name\` must be at most 64 characters, got 66\",\"param\":\"name\",\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\"}}","provider_name":"Meta","is_byok":false}}}
```

### 2. Disable Codex Apps

```bash
codex exec \
  -m meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor \
  --skip-git-repo-check \
  -c 'features.apps=false' \
  "Reply with exactly: hello"
```

Result:

```text
codex
hello
```

So the only meaningful change required to make the model work is:

```toml
[features]
apps = false
```

## Additional isolation

I also tested the following:

- Direct OpenRouter `/responses` request to `meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor`: works
- Direct OpenRouter request with reasoning enabled: works
- Clean `CODEX_HOME` with only the OpenRouter provider configured: works
- All manually configured MCPs disabled: still fails
- `features.plugins=false`: still fails
- `node_repl` disabled: still fails
- `features.apps=false`: works

This strongly isolates the issue to the Codex Apps tool surface rather than OpenRouter, Muse, reasoning, user MCPs, plugins, or `node_repl`.

## Likely cause

Codex sends namespaced tools in the Responses payload. Some Codex Apps namespaces/tool names appear to exceed Meta's maximum supported function name length once flattened.

For example, a flattened name of this shape:

```text
mcp__codex_apps__codex_document_control___execute_document_command
```

is 66 characters long.

Meta's backend rejects the entire request when any tool name exceeds 64 characters:

```text
`name` must be at most 64 characters, got 66
```

The raw Codex Responses request also contains nested namespace/tool structures, so the oversized name may only be produced when those namespaces are converted into provider-compatible function names.

## Expected behavior

Codex should ensure model-visible tool/function names comply with the target provider/model's constraints.

For providers with a 64-character maximum, Codex could:

- truncate and deterministically hash long tool names,
- use shorter generated aliases and map tool calls back internally,
- or otherwise normalize names before sending the request.

At minimum, enabling Codex Apps should not make a supported custom provider/model unusable because of generated tool names.

## Workaround

Currently:

```toml
[features]
apps = false
```

allows `meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` to work normally.

This is functional, but it disables the entire Codex Apps tool surface rather than only addressing the incompatible tool names.

body:
## What does this PR do?

`_OPENROUTER_ONLY` (`hermes_cli/models_catalog_static.py:51`) is documented as **"OpenRouter entries the Nous Portal does not carry"**, and `_PROVIDER_MODELS["nous"]` is derived by subtracting it from the curated OpenRouter list (`hermes_cli/models_catalog_static.py:157`):

```python
"nous": [mid for mid, _ in OPENROUTER_MODELS if mid not in _OPENROUTER_ONLY and not mid.endswith(":free")],
```

The set listed **four** muse-spark ids — the two plain SKUs and their two `-contributor` twins. But the Portal serves the plain SKUs. Keyless read of the live catalog:

```console
$ curl -s https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1/models \
    | jq -r '.data[] | select(.id|test("muse")) | "\(.id)\t\(.context_length)"'
meta/muse-spark-1.3     1048576
meta/muse-glimmer-30b   131072
meta/muse-glimmer-30b:batch     131072
meta/muse-spark-1.2     1048576
meta/muse-spark-1.1     1048576
```

403 ids in that catalog; `meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor` and `meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` are **not** among them, and neither are the other three members of the set (`anthropic/claude-opus-5-fast`, `anthropic/claude-opus-4.8-fast`, `openrouter/pareto-code`). So only the two plain muse-spark rows were misclassified.

The consequence: the `nous` row of the `/model` picker, the `hermes model` CLI flow, and the published catalog manifest — which is generated from the same list — all hid two models a Nous Portal user can actually reach, both with a 1,048,576-token context. Nothing else filters them back in: `restrict_to_nous_policy` narrows against the org's authenticated `GET /v1/models`, which carries them (`hermes_cli/models_pricing.py:326-342`).

The fix removes the two plain ids from `_OPENROUTER_ONLY`. The `-contributor` twins stay filtered — they really are OpenRouter-only, and they are the ones that carry the "vendor may train on your prompts" confirmation prompt (`website/docs/integrations/providers.md:354`).

`website/static/api/model-catalog.json` is regenerated with `scripts/build_model_catalog.py`, which `website/docs/reference/model-catalog.md:116` documents as the way to produce that file, and which `TestManifestMatchesInRepoLists` (`tests/hermes_cli/test_model_catalog.py:470`) enforces in CI. This matters at runtime, not just for CI: `get_curated_nous_model_ids()` (`hermes_cli/models.py:614-622`) prefers the fetched manifest over the in-repo snapshot, so without the regeneration the picker would keep serving the stale list. The regenerated diff is the two added nous entries plus the `updated_at` stamp the script always rewrites.

## Related Issue

No open issue. Found while auditing `_OPENROUTER_ONLY` against the live Portal catalog.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/models_catalog_static.py`: drop `meta/muse-spark-1.2` and `meta/muse-spark-1.3` from `_OPENROUTER_ONLY`; the comment now says the Portal does serve the plain SKUs and only the twins are listed.
- `website/static/api/model-catalog.json`: regenerated via `python scripts/build_model_catalog.py` — `nous` goes 42 → 44 models; `openrouter` untouched at 58.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_model_catalog.py`: new `TestPortalServedIdsReachTheNousPicker` with the four ids pinned as literals (no network in the test) — the two plain SKUs must be out of `_OPENROUTER_ONLY` and in both the curated list and the published manifest; the two `-contributor` twins must stay out of both.

## How to Test

1. On `main`, apply only the test file:

```console
$ scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_model_catalog.py
...
```

title: docs: add Meta Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Image 1.0
body:
Documents the two models added to the hub in Sozenta-Inc/vera#200. Docs only — no SDK code changes.

## Muse Spark 1.3

Same server-held key and Anthropic Messages endpoint as 1.1, so the existing reasoning-model guidance (generous `max_tokens`, `redacted_thinking` beside `text`, streaming recommended) carries over by reference rather than being restated. 1.1 is unchanged and still live; both are documented.

Wider input than 1.1: 1,048,576 context, plus video and PDF alongside text and images.

## The audio note is the part worth reviewing

Meta's model reference lists 1.3's input as "Text, image, video, audio\*, PDF". That asterisk is a **negative** footnote — audio understanding on this checkpoint is *"currently not fully supported"*, response quality *"may be degraded"*, and Meta redirects to **Spark 1.2** or **Muse Voice Transcribe**.

So the guide states plainly that audio is not offered on 1.3 and points at `moonshine` for speech-to-text. Declaring it would have advertised a capability Meta itself steers off this checkpoint.

Note this inverts the usual "newer is a superset" assumption: 1.1 is audio-capable and 1.3 is not.

## Muse Image 1.0

Documented as its **own connector**, not a Spark alias, and the guide says why — it is a different API family (Meta's OpenAI-compatible images endpoint, not Anthropic Messages), buffered rather than streaming, and it returns base64 at `data[0].b64_json`.

Because a proxy connector forwards the body **verbatim**, the guide is explicit that clients send the images shape (`model`, `prompt`, `n`) and *not* Anthropic `messages` — that verbatim-forward is what caused the original Spark 404, so it is called out rather than implied. It also notes that `GET /v1/stream/meta-image` does not exist.

A callout records that Meta *also* serves Muse Image conversationally on the Responses API (`/v1/responses`) for interleaving reference images across turns, and that this connector deliberately fronts only the one-off generations path — so a reader who wants the conversational shape knows it exists and knows it is an operator change, not a body tweak.

## Verification status

Every capability claim here is **documentation-derived, not response-derived**. I could not exercise the live Meta API: retrieving `META_MODEL_API_KEY` from Secrets Manager was blocked in my session, and `api.meta.ai` authenticates before routing (an unauthenticated POST to `/v1/foo` 401s exactly like a real path), so no endpoint could be confirmed to exist without credentials. Treat the wire details as unverified until someone runs a call with the key.

One thing I *could* measure without credentials: `/v1/messages` returns an Anthropic-shaped error envelope (`{"error":{…},"type":"error"}`) while every other `/v1` path returns an OpenAI-shaped one (`{"error":{"code":…,"param":…}}`). That confirms Meta special-cases the Messages path, which is consistent with the two models needing different connectors — but it is not proof that `/v1/images/generations` exists.

No trading, observe/paper, or risk-engine changes. ## Wiring - OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions at `https://api.meta.ai/v1` with Bearer auth. - Boot probe hits Meta's documented `GET /v1/models` the same way Groq/NVIDIA do. - Default id `muse-spark-1.3`, ladder walks to `muse-spark-1.1`. `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` is selectable via `META_MUSE_MODEL` / `MUSE_MODEL`. - Key aliases (first non-empty wins): `META_MUSE_API_KEY`, `MUSE_API_KEY`, Meta's official `MODEL_API_KEY`. ## Task chains - **chat / triage:** still Groq-first. Muse is a later fallback so a Muse-only deploy can still chat. - **research / agent / review / ideas:** Muse-first when a key is present, then the existing Anthropic → Kimi → NVIDIA → Groq → local cascade. - Unconfigured providers are skipped, so Groq-only and Anthropic-only deploys keep their previous order. ## Docs - `.env.example` documents the new vars (no real keys). - README + `docs/SETUP.md` note the chain, plus a short **safety loop** (paper-only, secrets in `.env`) and **iteration loop** (Muse journal/learning review in `observe` writes lessons only). ## Verification - `npm run typecheck` in `backend/` passed (`tsc --noEmit`). ## Out of scope Observe/paper defaults, kill switch, and order placement are untouched.
